about: What each IPA symbol is, in plain English, for a learner who has never read IPA: one entry per symbol on the 2020 IPA chart, plus the affricates and r-coloured vowels transcriptions write without a tie bar, letters with a mark that have a recording of their own, and the Pinyin letters with the IPA they stand for. Written once by hand and checked against Wikipedia's article for each sound (experiments/ipa-sounds/README.md); nothing here is generated per word. tests/unit/test_ipa_table.py holds the Pinyin rows to acervo/mandarin_ipa.py.

fields.symbol: the symbol as written; a diacritic or tone mark is the combining character alone
fields.example: for a diacritic or tone mark: the mark on a letter, as it is shown
fields.name: the chart's name for it
fields.how: how to make it, in one or two plain sentences
fields.like: the nearest English sound, with a word; null when English has none
fields.heard: a word in another language that has it, when English does not (or not clearly)
fields.aliases: other ways the same symbol is typed
fields.sound: the recording it plays, a file in sounds/ (credited in `recordings`), named by a digest of its bytes
fields.audio: phrases the recordings were searched for by on Wikimedia Commons (the experiment's apparatus)
fields.files: Commons files named outright as candidates (the experiment's apparatus)

notes.affricates: A stop released into a hiss, counted as one sound. The chart writes them with a tie bar (t͡s); most transcriptions, Acervo's Mandarin among them, leave it out.
notes.combinations: A letter with a mark that Commons has recorded as one sound. The panel plays it in place of the bare letter's recording; any other marked letter plays its bare letter, and the mark's text says what differs.
notes.diacritics: A mark changes the letter it is written on. The panel shows it with that letter.
notes.tones: Chao tone letters: each is a bar with a mark at a pitch from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). A run of them is one tone, read left to right as the pitch moves; a font joins them into one line.
notes.pinyin: Pinyin letters and the IPA acervo/mandarin_ipa.py writes for them (tests/unit/test_ipa_table.py holds the two together). `example` is a syllable that has the sound; its recording is Commons' Zh-<syllable>. A tone plays the recordings of the contour with its letters; the neutral tone names its own.

consonants.name: voiceless bilabial plosive
consonants.how: Close both lips, then open them, with no voice.
consonants.like: "p" in "spin". At the start of a word English adds a puff of air (pʰ), as in "pin".

consonants.name: voiced bilabial plosive
consonants.how: Like p, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

consonants.name: voiceless alveolar plosive
consonants.how: The tongue tip stops the air at the ridge behind the upper teeth, then lets go, with no voice.
consonants.like: "t" in "stop". English "top" adds a puff of air (tʰ).

consonants.name: voiced alveolar plosive
consonants.how: Like t, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

consonants.name: voiceless retroflex plosive
consonants.how: Like t, but with the tongue tip curled back to touch the roof of the mouth behind the ridge.
consonants.heard: Hindi ट, as in टमाटर ṭamāṭar (tomato).

consonants.name: voiced retroflex plosive
consonants.how: Like d, with the tongue tip curled back.
consonants.heard: Hindi ड, as in डाक ḍāk (mail).

consonants.name: voiceless palatal plosive
consonants.how: The middle of the tongue presses against the hard palate, where it is for "y", then lets go, with no voice.
consonants.like: Close to the "k" in "key", made further forward.
consonants.heard: Hungarian ty, as in tyúk (hen).

consonants.name: voiced palatal plosive
consonants.how: Like c, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.
consonants.like: Close to the "g" in "geese", made further forward.
consonants.heard: Hungarian gy, as in magyar (Hungarian).

consonants.name: voiceless velar plosive
consonants.how: The back of the tongue stops the air against the soft palate, then lets go, with no voice.
consonants.like: "k" in "skin". English "kin" adds a puff of air (kʰ).

consonants.name: voiced velar plosive
consonants.how: Like k, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

consonants.name: voiceless uvular plosive
consonants.how: Like k, but further back in the throat, with the back of the tongue against the uvula.
consonants.heard: Arabic ق, as in قلب qalb (heart).

consonants.name: voiced uvular plosive
consonants.how: Like q, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it. Rare.

consonants.name: glottal stop
consonants.how: The vocal folds shut and open again, a catch in the throat.
consonants.like: The catch in the middle of "uh-oh", or in place of the "t" in many speakers' "button".

consonants.name: bilabial nasal
consonants.how: Lips closed, and the air goes out through the nose: a hum.

consonants.name: labiodental nasal
consonants.how: An m made with the lower lip against the upper teeth.
consonants.like: The "m" in "symphony" or "comfort", said at normal speed.

consonants.name: alveolar nasal
consonants.how: The tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth, air through the nose.

consonants.name: retroflex nasal
consonants.how: An n with the tongue tip curled back to touch the roof of the mouth, behind the ridge.
consonants.heard: Swedish rn, as in barn (child).

consonants.name: palatal nasal
consonants.how: The middle of the tongue against the hard palate, air through the nose.
consonants.like: Close to the "ny" in "canyon", said as one sound.
consonants.heard: Spanish ñ, as in año (year); French gn, as in agneau (lamb).

consonants.name: velar nasal
consonants.how: The back of the tongue against the soft palate, air through the nose.

consonants.name: uvular nasal
consonants.how: Like ŋ, but further back, against the uvula.
consonants.heard: Spanish n before j in Spain, as in enjuto (shriveled). Japanese ん at the end of a word is often written ɴ.

consonants.name: voiced bilabial trill
consonants.how: The lips vibrate against each other as the air passes, with the voice on.
consonants.like: The "brrr" people say when they are cold.

consonants.name: alveolar trill
consonants.how: The tongue tip vibrates against the ridge behind the upper teeth, the rolled r.
consonants.heard: Spanish rr, as in perro (dog); Russian р, as in рыба (fish).

consonants.name: uvular trill
consonants.how: The uvula vibrates against the back of the tongue.
consonants.heard: The r of some German speakers, as in rot (red), and of some French dialects; most say ʁ instead.

consonants.name: labiodental flap
consonants.how: The lower lip flicks once against the upper teeth. Found in some languages of Africa.

consonants.name: alveolar tap
consonants.how: The tongue tip taps the ridge behind the upper teeth once, quickly.
consonants.heard: Spanish r between vowels, as in pero (but).
audio: dental and alveolar taps and flaps

consonants.name: retroflex flap
consonants.how: The tongue tip curls back and flicks forward once.
consonants.heard: Hindi ड़, as in बड़ा baṛā (big).

consonants.name: voiceless bilabial fricative
consonants.how: Blow through lips that almost touch, as when blowing out a candle.
consonants.heard: Japanese f, as in 富士 Fuji.

consonants.name: voiced bilabial fricative
consonants.how: Like ɸ, with the voice on, a soft b where the lips do not close.
consonants.heard: Spanish b or v between vowels, as in lobo (wolf).

consonants.name: voiceless labiodental fricative
consonants.how: The lower lip against the upper teeth, air pushed through.

consonants.name: voiced labiodental fricative
consonants.how: Like f, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

consonants.name: voiceless dental fricative
consonants.how: The tongue tip at the upper teeth, air pushed through.

consonants.name: voiced dental fricative
consonants.how: Like θ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

consonants.name: voiceless alveolar fricative
consonants.how: The tongue tip near the ridge behind the upper teeth, a hiss.

consonants.name: voiced alveolar fricative
consonants.how: Like s, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

consonants.name: voiceless postalveolar fricative
consonants.how: The tongue a little further back than for s, lips slightly pushed out.

consonants.name: voiced postalveolar fricative
consonants.how: Like ʃ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

consonants.name: voiceless retroflex fricative
consonants.how: Like "sh", but with the tongue tip curled back behind the ridge.
consonants.like: Close to "sh" in "shoe", with the tongue curled back.
consonants.heard: Mandarin sh, as in 书 shū (book); Russian ш, as in шар (ball).

consonants.name: voiced retroflex fricative
consonants.how: Like ʂ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.
consonants.like: Close to the "s" in "measure", with the tongue curled back.
consonants.heard: Russian ж, as in жук (beetle); Mandarin r, as in 热 rè (hot).

consonants.name: voiceless palatal fricative
consonants.how: Air hissing between the middle of the tongue and the hard palate, as for a whispered "y".
consonants.like: The "h" in "hue" for many British and Australian speakers, said with a hiss.
consonants.heard: German ch after front vowels, as in ich (I).

consonants.name: voiced palatal fricative
consonants.how: Like ç, with the voice on, a "y" with friction.
consonants.heard: Spanish y between vowels for many speakers, as in mayo (May).

consonants.name: voiceless velar fricative
consonants.how: Air hissing between the back of the tongue and the soft palate.
consonants.heard: German ch, as in Buch (book); Spanish j, as in jamón (ham); Russian х; Mandarin h, as in 好 hǎo (good).

consonants.name: voiced velar fricative
consonants.how: Like x, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.
consonants.heard: Spanish g between vowels, as in lago (lake); Greek γ, as in γάλα (milk).

consonants.name: voiceless uvular fricative
consonants.how: Like x, but further back, with the uvula.
consonants.heard: German ch after a, o or u, as in Dach (roof); Dutch ch, as in acht (eight); Spanish j in Spain, as in juego (game).

consonants.name: voiced uvular fricative
consonants.how: Like χ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.
consonants.heard: French r, as in rouge (red); German r, as in rot (red).

consonants.name: voiceless pharyngeal fricative
consonants.how: A strong, breathy h made by squeezing the throat.
consonants.heard: Arabic ح, as in حبيب ḥabīb (beloved).

consonants.name: voiced pharyngeal fricative
consonants.how: Like ħ, with the voice on; usually closer to a squeezed vowel than a hiss.
consonants.heard: Arabic ع, as in عرب ʿarab (Arabs).

consonants.name: voiceless glottal fricative
consonants.how: Air through the open throat, no shape in the mouth.

consonants.name: voiced glottal fricative
consonants.how: A breathy h with the voice on, as in a sigh.
consonants.like: The "h" in "behind" for many speakers, between two voiced sounds.
consonants.heard: Czech h, as in hora (mountain).

consonants.name: voiceless alveolar lateral fricative
consonants.how: Put the tongue where it is for l, and blow air past its sides with no voice.
consonants.heard: Welsh ll, as in Llanelli.

consonants.name: voiced alveolar lateral fricative
consonants.how: Like ɬ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.
consonants.heard: Zulu dl, as in dlala (play).

consonants.name: labiodental approximant
consonants.how: The lower lip near the upper teeth, softer than v, with no hiss.
consonants.like: Between "v" and "w": the lower lip near the upper teeth, but too loose to hiss.
consonants.heard: Dutch w, as in wat (what).

consonants.name: alveolar approximant
consonants.how: The tongue tip raised towards the ridge behind the teeth without touching it.

consonants.name: retroflex approximant
consonants.how: An r with the tongue tip curled back towards the roof of the mouth, without touching it.
consonants.heard: Mandarin r for many speakers, as in 人 rén (person).

consonants.name: palatal approximant
consonants.how: The middle of the tongue raised towards the hard palate.
consonants.like: "y" in "yes". It is never the English "j".

consonants.name: velar approximant
consonants.how: The back of the tongue raised towards the soft palate, like a w with spread lips.

consonants.name: alveolar lateral approximant
consonants.how: The tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth, air past its sides.
audio: dental alveolar and postalveolar lateral approximants

consonants.name: retroflex lateral approximant
consonants.how: An l with the tongue tip curled back to touch the roof of the mouth, behind the ridge.
consonants.heard: Swedish rl, as in sorl (murmur).

consonants.name: palatal lateral approximant
consonants.how: An l made with the middle of the tongue against the hard palate.
consonants.like: Close to the "lli" in "million", said as one sound.
consonants.heard: Italian gl, as in figlio (son).

consonants.name: velar lateral approximant
consonants.how: An l made with the back of the tongue against the soft palate. Rare.

consonants.name: voiceless labial-velar fricative
consonants.how: A w with no voice, blown through rounded lips.
consonants.like: The "wh" in "which", for speakers who say it differently from "witch".

consonants.name: voiced labial-velar approximant
consonants.how: Rounded lips with the back of the tongue raised.

consonants.name: voiced labial-palatal approximant
consonants.how: A "y" said with rounded lips, as if "y" and "w" at once.
consonants.heard: French u before a vowel, as in huit (eight).

consonants.name: voiceless epiglottal fricative
consonants.how: A harsh hiss made deep in the throat, below ħ. Rare.

consonants.name: voiced epiglottal fricative
consonants.how: Like ʜ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it. Rare.

consonants.name: epiglottal plosive
consonants.how: A stop made deep in the throat with the epiglottis. Rare.

consonants.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative
consonants.how: Between s and sh, with the tongue flat and the lips spread.
consonants.heard: Mandarin x, as in 谢谢 xièxie (thanks); Japanese し shi; Russian щ (long).

consonants.name: voiced alveolo-palatal fricative
consonants.how: Like ɕ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.
consonants.heard: Polish ź, as in źle (badly).

consonants.name: alveolar lateral flap
consonants.how: One quick flick of the tongue, between an l and a tapped r.
consonants.heard: Japanese r for many speakers, as in ラーメン rāmen.

consonants.name: voiceless dorso-palatal velar fricative
consonants.how: Two hisses at once, sh-like and at the back of the mouth. Swedish only.
consonants.heard: Swedish sj, as in sju (seven).

consonants.name: velarized alveolar lateral approximant
consonants.how: An l with the back of the tongue raised as well, a "dark" l.
consonants.heard: Russian л, as in лампа (lamp).

affricates.name: voiceless alveolar affricate
affricates.how: t and s run together as one sound, with no gap between them.
affricates.like: "ts" in "cats", but able to start a word.
affricates.heard: German z, as in Zeit (time); Mandarin z, as in 在 zài; Russian ц.

affricates.name: voiced alveolar affricate
affricates.how: d and z run together as one sound, with no gap between them.

affricates.name: voiceless postalveolar affricate
affricates.how: t and sh run together as one sound, with no gap between them.

affricates.name: voiced postalveolar affricate
affricates.how: d and the "s" of "measure" run together as one sound.

affricates.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate
affricates.how: A t released into ɕ, the tongue flat and the lips spread.
affricates.heard: Mandarin j, as in 家 jiā (home); Polish ć, as in być (to be); Japanese ち chi.
files: Voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate by Chinese native speaker.ogg

affricates.name: voiced alveolo-palatal affricate
affricates.how: Like tɕ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.

affricates.name: voiceless retroflex affricate
affricates.how: A t released into ʂ, the tongue tip curled back.
affricates.like: Close to "ch" in "church", with the tongue curled back.
affricates.heard: Mandarin zh, as in 中 zhōng (middle); Polish cz, as in czas (time).

affricates.name: voiced retroflex affricate
affricates.how: Like ʈʂ, but with the voice on: the throat buzzes while you say it.
affricates.like: Close to "j" in "jam", with the tongue curled back.

affricates.name: voiceless labiodental affricate
affricates.how: p released straight into f, as one sound: the lips close, then open only as far as for f.

combinations.name: aspirated voiceless alveolar plosive
combinations.how: t followed by a puff of air you can feel on your hand.
combinations.heard: Mandarin t, as in 他 tā (he).

combinations.name: aspirated voiceless velar plosive
combinations.how: k followed by a puff of air you can feel on your hand.
combinations.heard: Mandarin k, as in 看 kàn (to look).

combinations.name: aspirated voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate
combinations.how: tɕ followed by a puff of air you can feel on your hand.
combinations.like: Close to "ch" in "cheap", with the tongue tip down behind the lower teeth.
combinations.heard: Mandarin q, as in 七 qī (seven).
files: Voiceless alveolo palatal affricate with Aspiration by Chinese native speaker.ogg

combinations.name: nasalized open-mid front unrounded vowel
combinations.how: ɛ with air through the nose as well as the mouth.

combinations.name: nasalized open-mid back rounded vowel
combinations.how: ɔ with air through the nose as well as the mouth.

combinations.name: nasalized open back unrounded vowel
combinations.how: ɑ with air through the nose as well as the mouth.
combinations.heard: French an or en, as in blanc (white).

vowels.name: close front unrounded vowel
vowels.how: The tongue high and forward, lips spread.
vowels.like: "ee" in "see", without the slight "y" glide English adds at its end.

vowels.name: close front rounded vowel
vowels.how: Say "ee", then round the lips as for "oo" without moving the tongue.
vowels.heard: French u, as in tu (you); German ü, as in über; Mandarin ü, as in 绿 lǜ (green).

vowels.name: close central unrounded vowel
vowels.how: Like "ee" with the tongue pulled back to the middle.

vowels.name: close central rounded vowel
vowels.how: Like "oo" with the tongue pushed forward to the middle.
vowels.like: The "oo" in "goose" in many younger British and Australian speakers.

vowels.name: close back unrounded vowel
vowels.how: "oo" without rounding the lips: keep them spread, as for "ee".
vowels.heard: Turkish ı, as in kız (girl); Korean ㅡ.

vowels.name: close back rounded vowel
vowels.how: The tongue high and back, the lips rounded and pushed forward.
vowels.like: "oo" in "food", without the slight "w" glide English adds at its end.

vowels.name: near-close near-front unrounded vowel
vowels.how: A relaxed "ee", slightly lower and shorter.

vowels.name: near-close near-front rounded vowel
vowels.how: ɪ with rounded lips: say the "i" of "sit", then round the lips without moving the tongue.
vowels.heard: German ü in a short syllable, as in hübsch (pretty).

vowels.name: near-close near-back rounded vowel
vowels.how: A relaxed "oo", slightly lower, with the lips only lightly rounded.

vowels.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel
vowels.how: The tongue a little lower than for "ee", lips spread.
vowels.like: The "a" in "say", without the glide into "y".
vowels.heard: French é, as in été (summer); German ee, as in See (lake).

vowels.name: close-mid front rounded vowel
vowels.how: Say e (the "a" of "say" without its glide), then round the lips without moving the tongue.
vowels.heard: French eu, as in peu (little); German ö, as in schön (beautiful).

vowels.name: close-mid central unrounded vowel
vowels.how: Between e and the "uh" of ə, a little higher than ə. Rare as a sound of its own.

vowels.name: close-mid central rounded vowel
vowels.how: ɘ with rounded lips.
vowels.heard: Swedish u in a short syllable, as in full (full).

vowels.name: close-mid back unrounded vowel
vowels.how: An "o" with the lips spread instead of rounded.
vowels.heard: Mandarin e, as in 饿 è (hungry) and 喝 hē (drink).

vowels.name: close-mid back rounded vowel
vowels.how: The tongue back, lips rounded, a little lower than "oo".
vowels.like: The "o" in "go", without the glide into "w".
vowels.heard: French eau (water); German o, as in so.

vowels.name: mid central vowel
vowels.how: The tongue at rest in the middle of the mouth, the "schwa".

vowels.name: open-mid front unrounded vowel
vowels.how: The tongue a little lower than for e, the mouth a little more open.

vowels.name: open-mid front rounded vowel
vowels.how: Say ɛ (the "e" of "bed"), then round the lips without moving the tongue.
vowels.heard: French eu, as in peur (fear); German ö, as in Hölle (hell).

vowels.name: open-mid central unrounded vowel
vowels.how: A relaxed vowel in the middle of the mouth, lower than ə.
vowels.like: The "ir" in British "bird" (written ɜː, since it is long).

vowels.name: open-mid central rounded vowel
vowels.how: ɜ with rounded lips. Rare.

vowels.name: open-mid back unrounded vowel
vowels.how: The tongue low and back, the lips spread, the mouth fairly open.
vowels.like: The "u" in American "cup"; many British speakers say it further forward (ɐ).

vowels.name: open-mid back rounded vowel
vowels.how: The tongue low and back, the lips rounded, the mouth fairly open.
vowels.like: The "ou" in British "thought" (written ɔː, since it is long).

vowels.name: near-open front unrounded vowel
vowels.how: The mouth wide open, the tongue low and forward.

vowels.name: near-open central vowel
vowels.how: A short, relaxed "ah" in the middle of the mouth.
vowels.like: The "u" in "cup" in many British speakers.
vowels.heard: German -er, as in besser (better); Portuguese a, as in cama (bed).

vowels.name: open front unrounded vowel
vowels.how: The mouth wide open, the tongue low and forward. Many transcriptions use it for the "ah" of the middle of the mouth.
vowels.like: Between the "a" in "cat" and the "a" in "father".

vowels.name: open front rounded vowel
vowels.how: a with rounded lips. Rare.

vowels.name: open back unrounded vowel
vowels.how: The mouth wide open, the tongue low and back.

vowels.name: open back rounded vowel
vowels.how: ɑ with the lips rounded, the mouth still wide open.

vowels.name: r-coloured mid central vowel
vowels.how: ə said with the tongue curled or bunched as for an American r.
vowels.heard: Mandarin er, as in 儿 ér (child).

vowels.name: r-coloured open-mid central vowel
vowels.how: ɜ said with the tongue curled or bunched, as for an American r.

diacritics.name: voiceless
diacritics.how: Said without the voice: the throat does not buzz.

diacritics.name: voiced
diacritics.how: Said with the voice on: the throat buzzes.

diacritics.name: aspirated
diacritics.how: Followed by a puff of air. English "pin" is pʰ and "spin" is p. In Mandarin the puff is what tells Pinyin p (pʰ) from b (p).

diacritics.name: more rounded
diacritics.how: Lips rounded more than usual.

diacritics.name: less rounded
diacritics.how: Lips rounded less than usual.

diacritics.name: advanced
diacritics.how: The tongue a little further forward.

diacritics.name: retracted
diacritics.how: The tongue a little further back.

diacritics.name: centralized
diacritics.how: Moved towards the middle of the mouth.

diacritics.name: mid-centralized
diacritics.how: Moved towards ə, the relaxed middle vowel.

diacritics.name: syllabic
diacritics.how: A consonant that makes a syllable by itself, with no vowel. The "n" in "button" (ˈbʌtn̩). Mandarin shì is ʂɻ̩: its vowel is a held r-sound.

diacritics.name: non-syllabic
diacritics.how: A vowel that does not make a syllable of its own: it glides into or out of its neighbour. The "i̯" of ai̯ is the "y" at the end of "eye", the "u̯" of ou̯ the "w" at the end of "go".

diacritics.name: rhoticity
diacritics.how: Said with an r colour, the tongue curled or bunched as for an American r. Mandarin erhua adds it to a syllable.

diacritics.name: breathy voiced
diacritics.how: Voice with a lot of breath, a murmur.

diacritics.name: creaky voiced
diacritics.how: A low, creaking voice, as at the end of a tired sentence.

diacritics.name: linguolabial
diacritics.how: The tongue tip against the upper lip.

diacritics.name: labialized
diacritics.how: With rounded lips, a "w" colour. The "qu" in "queen" is kʷ.

diacritics.name: palatalized
diacritics.how: With the middle of the tongue raised, a "y" colour. Russian soft consonants, as in нет (nʲet, no).

diacritics.name: velarized
diacritics.how: With the back of the tongue raised.

diacritics.name: pharyngealized
diacritics.how: With the throat squeezed. Arabic "emphatic" consonants.

diacritics.name: velarized or pharyngealized
diacritics.how: A dark sound, made deep in the mouth or throat. The dark l, ɫ, has it built in.

diacritics.name: raised
diacritics.how: The tongue a little higher than usual.

diacritics.name: lowered
diacritics.how: The tongue a little lower than usual. Spanish e and o are e̞ and o̞, between e and ɛ, o and ɔ.

diacritics.name: advanced tongue root
diacritics.how: The root of the tongue pushed forward, widening the throat.

diacritics.name: retracted tongue root
diacritics.how: The root of the tongue pulled back.

diacritics.name: dental
diacritics.how: Made against the teeth rather than the ridge behind them. Spanish, French and Russian t and d.

diacritics.name: apical
diacritics.how: Made with the very tip of the tongue.

diacritics.name: laminal
diacritics.how: Made with the flat blade of the tongue, just behind the tip.

diacritics.name: nasalized
diacritics.how: Air through the nose as well as the mouth. French bon (bɔ̃) and vin (vɛ̃); Portuguese mãe (mɐ̃j̃).

diacritics.name: nasal release
diacritics.how: Released through the nose, as the "dn" in "sudden".

diacritics.name: lateral release
diacritics.how: Released past the sides of the tongue, as the "dl" in "middle".

diacritics.name: no audible release
diacritics.how: Stopped and never released, as the "p" at the end of a quick "yep".

diacritics.name: tie bar
diacritics.how: The two letters it joins are one sound.

suprasegmentals.name: primary stress
suprasegmentals.how: The syllable after it is stressed. "about" is əˈbaʊt.

suprasegmentals.name: secondary stress
suprasegmentals.how: The syllable after it has a lighter stress. "pronunciation" is prəˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən.

suprasegmentals.name: long
suprasegmentals.how: The sound before it is held longer. "see" is siː.

suprasegmentals.name: half-long
suprasegmentals.how: The sound before it is a little longer than usual.

suprasegmentals.name: extra-short
suprasegmentals.how: The sound is shorter than usual.

suprasegmentals.name: syllable break
suprasegmentals.how: A new syllable starts here: "hotel" is hoʊ.ˈtɛl.

suprasegmentals.name: minor (foot) group
suprasegmentals.how: A short pause or break in the phrase.

suprasegmentals.name: linking
suprasegmentals.how: No break between the words it joins.

suprasegmentals.name: downstep
suprasegmentals.how: The pitch steps down from here on.

suprasegmentals.name: upstep
suprasegmentals.how: The pitch steps up from here on.

contours.name: high level
contours.how: The pitch stays high and even, as if singing one note.

contours.name: rising
contours.how: The pitch rises from the middle to the top, as in a surprised "what?".

contours.name: dipping
contours.how: The pitch dips low, then rises. In running speech it often stays low (˨˩).

contours.name: falling
contours.how: The pitch falls from the top to the bottom, as in a firm "No!".
contours.mandarin: 4th tone, as in 骂 mà (to scold).

initials.how: Like "p" in "spin": no puff of air. It is not voiced like English b, but sounds close to it.
"p" in "pin", with a strong puff of air.
"m" in "man", the same as in English.
"f" in "fan", the same as in English.
Like "t" in "stop": no puff of air. To English ears it often sounds like a "d", though the voice is not on.
"t" in "top", with a strong puff of air.
"n" in "no", the same as in English.
"l" in "leaf", the same as in English.
Like "k" in "skin": no puff of air. To English ears it often sounds like a "g", though the voice is not on.
"k" in "kin", with a strong puff of air.
A hiss at the back of the mouth, like a soft "ch" in Scottish "loch". Not the English "h".
Like "j" in "jeep" with the tongue tip down behind the lower teeth. No puff of air.
Like "ch" in "cheap" with the tongue tip down, and a puff of air. Never "kw".
Between "s" and "sh", the tongue tip down and the lips spread. Never "ks".
Like "j" in "judge" with the tongue tip curled back. No puff of air.
Like "ch" in "church" with the tongue tip curled back, and a puff of air.
Like "sh" in "shoe", with the tongue tip curled back towards the roof of the mouth, which makes it sound deeper.
Like the "s" in "measure" with the tongue curled back; many speakers make it close to an English "r".
Like "ds" in "beds": no puff of air. Never the English "z".
Like "ts" in "cats", with a strong puff of air. Never "k" or "s".
"s" in "see", the same as in English.

finals.how: An open "ah", like the "a" in "father" but a little shorter.
Only after b, p, m and f, where it is said "uo": bo is pu̯o, like "bwo".
An "o" with spread lips, close to the "u" in "duh" said far back. Not the English "e".
The "ar" in American "are", or the "er" in "butter".
Like "eye": an open "ah" gliding up into a short "ee".
Like "ay" in "say": an "e" gliding into a short "ee". Never the "ee" of "receive".
Like "ow" in "cow": an open "ah" gliding into a short "oo". Not the "ay-oh" of "chaos".
Like "o" in "go": an "o" gliding into a short "oo". Not the "ou" of "out" or "you".
"ahn": the "a" of "father" followed by n. Not the "a" of "man".
The "en" in "taken", with a relaxed vowel.
"ahng", the "a" of "father" and the "ng" of "sing".
The "ung" in "sung", with a relaxed vowel.
The "oo" of "foot" and the "ng" of "sing".
"ee" in "see". After zh, ch, sh, r, z, c and s it is a different sound: see -i below.
"ya" as in "yard": a short "ee" gliding into an open "ah". Written ya at the start of a syllable, as in 鸭 yā (duck).
"ye" as in "yes", with the e a little tenser, closer to the "a" of "say". Written ye at the start of a syllable, as in 也 yě (also).
"yow" as in "yowl": a short "ee", then "ow" as in "cow". Written yao at the start of a syllable, as in 要 yào (to want).
Spelt iu, said "yo" as in "yo-yo": the full spelling is iou.
"yen": a short "ee", then "en" as in "ten". The a here is not "ah", the most common slip. Written yan at the start of a syllable, as in 烟 yān (smoke).
"een" as in "seen", but short. Written yin at the start of a syllable, as in 音 yīn (sound).
"yahng": a short "ee", then the "a" of "father" and the "ng" of "sing". Unlike in ian, the a stays "ah". Written yang at the start of a syllable, as in 羊 yáng (sheep).
"ing" as in "sing"; many speakers slip a light "uh" before the ng. Written ying at the start of a syllable, as in 鹰 yīng (eagle).
"yoong": a short "ee", then the "oo" of "foot" and the "ng" of "sing". Written yong at the start of a syllable, as in 用 yòng (to use).
A short "ee" gliding into "o", like "yo". Only in the exclamation 哟 yō (oh!), written yo.
"oo" in "food". After j, q, x and y it is spelt u but said ü (y).
"wah": a short "oo" gliding quickly into the "a" of "father". Written wa at the start of a syllable, as in 娃 wá (baby).
"waw", the w and an "o" without a glide.
"why": a short "oo", then the "eye" of ai, in one quick glide. Written wai at the start of a syllable, as in 外 wài (outside).
Spelt ui, said "way": the full spelling is uei.
"wahn": a short "oo" gliding into "ahn". After j, q, x and y the same spelling is üan instead. Written wan at the start of a syllable, as in 万 wàn (ten thousand).
Spelt un, said "wun" with a relaxed vowel: the full spelling is uen.
"wahng": a short "oo" gliding into the "a" of "father" and the "ng" of "sing". Written wang at the start of a syllable, as in 王 wáng (king).
A short "oo" gliding into the "ung" of "sung". Only on its own, written weng, as in 嗡 wēng (to buzz).
Say "ee" with rounded lips, like French u. Spelt u after j, q, x and y.
ü gliding into a tense "e". Spelt ue after j, q, x and y.
ü gliding into "en" as in "bed". Spelt uan after j, q, x and y.
ü followed by n. Spelt un after j, q, x and y.
Not "ee": hold the tongue where it was for zh, ch, sh or r and let the voice buzz through it.
Not "ee": hold the tongue where it was for z, c or s and let the voice buzz through it, a voiced "zzz".
An r curled onto the end of the syllable, as in 哪儿 nǎr (where). It can swallow an n or i before it.

tones.how: High and level, held steady near the top of your voice, as if singing one note.
Rising from the middle to the top, as in a surprised "what?".
Low, dipping, then rising; in running speech often just low.
Falling sharply from high to low, as in a firm "No!".
Neutral: short and light, its pitch set by the tone before it. IPA writes no tone letter.
